text:
marta: Heads-up — opened a docs PR because the /v1/embeddings example in the API reference still shows `input` as a single string, but the runtime expects an array for batch requests. This is causing confusion in support tickets. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4687 :eyes:

kevin: can you paste the snippet that's wrong? iirc we changed the API to accept both but examples should show the array for batch calls.

marta: sure — current example in the page is:
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "open-embed-1",
  "input": "hello world"
}
```
That suggests single-item usage only. The client SDKs and server validate prefer `input: [..]` for batching. Proposed replacement:
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "open-embed-1",
  "input": ["hello world", "how are you?"]
}
```
Also added a short note about server returning `data: [{embedding: [...]}]` and the per-item order guarantee.

kevin: good catch. can you also add a one-line migration note for older clients that accepted a string? e.g. "string inputs will be wrapped into an array by newer SDKs; servers will normalize to array in responses" — helps internal teams.

marta: added the migration paragraph in the PR description. i also changed the JS snippet under the SDK examples to use `await client.embeddings.create({ model, input: [... ] })` and included the returned array parsing example.

docs-bot: CI check failed on the PR — lint error in openapi examples: `components.schemas.EmbeddingsRequest.input` example type mismatch (expected array, found string). See build log: https://ci.redwood-inference/1234/logs/789 :warning:

oliver: pinging @kevin — the docs linter will block merge until the YAML example is updated. kevin can you push the fix?

kevin: on it. i'll update the OpenAPI example and the code-snippet generator template (js) to ensure it always emits arrays for `input`. also will add a one-line note in the response schema that `data` is an array of embeddings with stable ordering.

marta: thanks — after CI passes can someone add a tiny test that fetches the rendered page and asserts the example contains "\"input\": [\"hello world\"]"? avoids regressions.

kevin: adding the test now. will re-run docs build and link the passing green CI here.

docs-bot: CI passed on branch fix/embeds-request-examples — build 456 succeeded :white_check_mark: https://ci.redwood-inference/1234/builds/456

oliver: merged. tiny follow-up: update the migration guide under /docs/migration/2025-embed-array.md to mention SDK auto-wrap behaviour and an example of converting single-string payloads in Python and Go. i'll file a quick follow-up PR.

marta: perfect — closing the thread. thanks all :heart:
